newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks close down again in nervous session.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks close down again in nervous session.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange ended lower for the third consecutive session in nervous trade dominated by the erratic Volcan mining stock.
Traders said trade Friday would likely remain volatile.

"Today, Volcan has had so many ups and downs, that it represented half of the bolsa's movement and that hurt all the mining sector with some exceptions like Southern," said Interfip broker Gilbert Chauny.
According to preliminary data, the General Index fell 1.09 percent to 2,041.42 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index fell 0.94 percent to 2,941.64.

Volcan was buoyed by the recent purchase of state mining company Centromin's Mahr Tunel unit, which turned it into the country's leading zinc producer. The stock soared 10 percent in early trade, but quickly lost those gains and ended 10 percent down at 24.30 soles on 815,183 shares.
Most miners followed suit, with Morococha ending off 9.98 percent to 5.77 soles, Buenaventura down 4.47 percent to 19.00 soles, and Perubar losing 7.93 percent to 7.66 percent.
But Southern Peru Copper bucked the sector's trend to make a 0.80 percent gain to 18.95 soles.
Total volume was 52 million soles ($20 million) on 2,072 trades as 48 shares fell, 29 were flat and 16 rose.
Brokers said that, apart from the speculative trading of Volcan, the market was also influenced by some negative recommendations from foreign investment banks.
"Two investment banks have recommended selling positions in some shares such as the miners Milpo and Arcata," said Pablo Navarro, of Fortuna brokerage.
Milpo lost 5.88 percent to 32.00 soles, while Arcata fell 0.21 percent to 2.19 soles.
